page: Microsoft Azure D48ls_v6 is a compute-focused general-purpose virtual machine within the Dlsv6 series, configured with 48 vCPUs and 96 GB of system memory. Driven by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor running up to 4.2 GHz across 24 physical cores (two threads per core), the instance allocates a dedicated 2 GB of memory per vCPU. Hardware capabilities include a massive 260 MB L3 cache alongside advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX Tile, and AMX INT8, optimizing execution for vectorized math, cryptography, and matrix operations.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong tier placement across computational and data-handling workloads. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 62,325.35 and Geekbench multi-core score of 20,088.0, with exceptional marks in image processing (20,338.0, placing in the top 10 percent) and Clang software compilation (43,827.0). Memory throughput remains strong under heavy loads, posting 249.73 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 102.08 GB/sec in large-block write operations. In operational throughput evaluations, it delivers 64.82 million Redis SET operations per second and handles 78.25 GB/sec in static web serving.

Architecturally, the instance prioritizes raw compute capacity over memory footprint, making it cost-efficient for core-intensive tasks that do not require standard 4:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratios. However, this design presents clear tradeoffs: memory-heavy databases may experience headroom limits, and the server includes zero local ephemeral disk storage, requiring external premium network storage for persistent or scratch filesystems. Additionally, graphics accelerators are absent, though AMX instructions enable capable CPU-based inference, demonstrated by 243.97 tokens per second on 7B parameter LLM prompt processing.
The D48ls_v6 is best suited for compute-heavy batch processing, multi-threaded CI/CD compilation pipelines, web tier fleets, and CPU-driven AI inference workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure D48ls_v6 is a low-memory variant of the Dlsv6 general-purpose family, provisioned with 48 dedicated vCPUs, 24 physical cores, and 96 GB of RAM on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor reaching 4.2 GHz. Featuring 260 MB of L3 cache, AVX-512, and Intel AMX matrix extensions, the hardware is tuned for dense computational throughput rather than massive memory allocation, operating at a 2 GB per core ratio. Benchmark evaluations show top-quartile performance in compilation, image manipulation, static web throughput (78.25 GB/sec), and Redis throughput (64.82 million operations per second). With no onboard local disk storage and zero discrete GPUs, the instance relies on remote network storage for disk operations. This profile makes the instance highly cost-efficient for thread-dense batch workloads, CI/CD runners, network-facing microservices, and CPU-based lightweight machine learning inference.
